chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer during travel while I was walking. He said, 'Nod with your head and make the prostration lower than the bowing.'

key_terms.أَوْمِ إِيمَاءً: Nod with your head (a method of prayer while walking)

ai.seo_question: How should one perform the travel prayer while walking according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi establishes the permissibility of performing the four-rak'ah prayer shortened to two while walking (salat al-musafir bi-l-mashi), a practice rooted in the Prophet's own conduct during journeys. The Imam’s instruction to lower the prostration relative to the bowing highlights the physical adjustments required to maintain the essential pillars of prayer while in motion, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of facilitating worship during travel without compromising its validity.
